readings.query:
-- Three defensible readings of "revenue", from the same rows.
SELECT
  SUM(o.amount) AS every_order,
  SUM(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'completed') AS completed_orders,
  SUM(o.amount) FILTER (
    WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND NOT c.is_test
  ) AS governed_net_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c USING (customer_id);

compiled.sql:
SELECT SUM(o.amount) AS net_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
  AND NOT c.is_test;

ready.yaml:
models:
  - name: fct_orders
    description: >
      One row per order. For revenue, use the net_revenue metric,
      which excludes refunded and cancelled orders and test accounts.
    config:
      access: public
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Primary key.
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: status
        description: Lifecycle state at the latest load.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [completed, refunded, cancelled]

unique.sql:
SELECT order_id AS unique_field, COUNT(*) AS n_records
FROM fct_orders
WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY order_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

accepted_values.sql:
WITH all_values AS (
  SELECT status AS value_field, COUNT(*) AS n_records
  FROM fct_orders
  GROUP BY status
)
SELECT * FROM all_values
WHERE value_field NOT IN ('completed', 'refunded', 'cancelled');

ready.description: which excludes refunded and cancelled orders and test accounts.

asWritten.sql:
SELECT SUM(o.amount) AS net_revenue
FROM fct_orders o
JOIN customers c USING (customer_id)
WHERE o.status NOT IN ('refunded', 'cancelled')
  AND NOT c.is_test;

candidates.label: A different join and aliases
candidates.sql:
SELECT SUM(ord.amount) AS revenue
FROM customers cust
JOIN orders ord
  ON ord.customer_id = cust.customer_id
 AND ord.status = 'completed'
WHERE cust.is_test = FALSE;

candidates.label: Completed orders only

withoutTest.sql:
DELETE FROM orders
WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE is_test);

review.compiledAsWritten:
select order_id, order_date, amount
from analytics.raw_orders
where order_date > (select max(order_date) from fct_orders)
review.compiledReviewed:
select order_id, order_date, amount
from analytics.raw_orders
where order_date > (select max(order_date) - interval '3 days' from fct_orders)

merge.sql:
MERGE INTO fct_orders t
USING batch s ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET order_date = s.order_date, amount = s.amount
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (s.order_id, s.order_date, s.amount);
